patch_description: The previous program spent its whole budget on beam-search restarts and greedy constructions but never refined the best solutions found. The key insight is that beam search gets you close quickly, while iterated local search (ILS) with insertion moves — relocating a transaction to every other position — exploits the structure of conflict delays far better than more randomized restarts. This design: (1) spends ~30% of the budget on greedy+beam constructions for diverse starting points, (2) spends the remaining ~70% on ILS where each iteration applies a best-improvement insertion sweep over the current solution, followed by random perturbation (random 3-relocation) when stuck, with acceptance of only improving solutions and restarts from the second-best candidate if stagnation persists. Full-sequence cost evaluation keeps correctness identical to the original interface.
